help.chat-photos.note4: With no signal, the photo waits on the phone with what you said it is, and is filed by itself when the signal comes back. Its card then says it was filed on the phone with no signal.
help.chat-photos.note5: Why filed, not sent: a photo passed round a chat could be of anything. Filed to its load or parcel — with who filed it, when, and a fingerprint — it can be relied on in a claim.
help.chat-photos.note6: The photo buttons are there only for somebody who is part of that load or parcel.
help.upload-refused.title: When a photo or a file will not upload
help.upload-refused.summary: No photo or file is refused without a word. A photo is made smaller on your phone before it is sent, and a PDF or a spreadsheet shows its limit beside the button that chooses it. If one cannot go, the app says why where you chose it: its size, the most, and what to do.
help.upload-refused.step1: A photo, however large: choose it as it is. The phone makes it smaller before it is sent.
help.upload-refused.step2: A picture the phone cannot open — some very large ones, and some kinds: the app says so. Take a photo with the camera instead, or choose a smaller one.
help.upload-refused.step3: A PDF too large: choose a smaller one, or take a photo of the paper instead. A photo is made smaller; a PDF cannot be.
help.upload-refused.step4: A spreadsheet too large: send only the sheet with the rows on it, or copy the rows and paste them instead.
help.upload-refused.step5: A voice message too large: record a shorter one, or type the message.
help.upload-refused.step6: “The photo did not go — tap to try again”, or “It did not go. Try again.”: the file was fine, but it did not reach us, usually for lack of signal. Try again once there is signal.
help.upload-refused.note1: A profile photo works the same: any photo, made smaller on the phone. If it cannot be used, the sheet says why, under the button that chose it.
help.upload-refused.note2: A file of the wrong kind is refused with a word too: a photo is asked for a photo, a PDF or a photo for a paper, and a spreadsheet for a sheet of orders or a packing list.
help.upload-refused.note3: Why a photo is made smaller: a phone camera’s picture is several megabytes, and a smaller one goes faster and costs less data.
help.car-messages.title: Hear your messages in the car
help.car-messages.summary: With the SeeBuyGet Driver app from Google Play and your phone connected to Android Auto, the car reads aloud the messages from the people in your chats about loads, and you answer by voice — the phone stays in its holder.
help.car-messages.step1: Install the SeeBuyGet Driver app from Google Play, open it, and sign in with your PIN as you always do.
help.car-messages.step2: Tap your picture, then “Settings”, and tap “Messages in the car”. Type your PIN and tap “Turn it on”.
help.car-messages.step3: The phone opens the Driver app’s own screen for a moment, then comes back. Settings says “Waiting for the phone” until the phone has answered, then “On for this phone”.
help.car-messages.step4: In the car, with the phone connected to Android Auto, a new message is announced. Ask the car to read it, then answer by voice: the car reads your answer back before it is sent.
help.car-messages.step5: To stop it, open the same row in Settings and tap “Turn it off”. Nothing else is asked.
help.car-messages.note1: Only conversations are read aloud. Offers of work, prices and settlements stay on the phone: open the app when you have stopped.
help.car-messages.note2: A voice message or a photo is not played in the car: the car says one arrived, and to open the app when you stop.
help.car-messages.note3: Your answer arrives as a text message marked “Sent from the car”, and is refused for the same reasons as a typed one — a conversation that is closed, or too many messages in an hour. The car then says it was not sent.
help.car-messages.note4: No “Messages in the car” row in Settings? It is there only in the SeeBuyGet Driver app from Google Play, not in a browser, and only on a phone your PIN works on. On a phone with Android 8 or older it says “Needs Android 9 or newer.”: the car part does not run there.
help.car-messages.note5: It turns itself off when your PIN is changed or replaced, when this phone is forgotten under “Settings › Phones and browsers”, or when your number moves. Turn it on again in Settings.
help.car-messages.note6: Why it is safe to leave on: Google’s Firebase only wakes the phone to say that a chat has news — never the words, and never who wrote them. The phone then fetches the message from SeeBuyGet.
help.car-messages.note7: While it is on, a chat message comes to the phone once — as the car’s own notification, with Reply and Mark as read — and not also as a notice from the app. It is still in the bell.
